description: plx.find over the stored word index of captured text (store v8, ontology/text_index.py; decision 2026-10-18-projection-store-v6 rebuild rules), measured on the same live captures and served state as ontology.mentions (the same probe argv: a GET-only Portal sync, one GET-only BC capture pass and one bounded Graph-delta capture of the allowlisted purchase-order@ mailbox, projected with the host's post_project steps, text_index among them). After the build, scripts/ontology_projection_probe.py mail_text_find_checks samples up to 50 stored mail text chunks (Email and Attachment fields: body, attachment text), queries the served host's plx.find (operating.host Host.served_tools) with the chunk's three longest plain words as the capture principal, and counts a hit only when a candidate is the chunk's own object cited to its field's citation and field path. The same query as probe:mail-withheld-reader (granted the records but not the mail) must be served no mail object. Pass = text_find_missed 0 (no complete answer without the sampled document), text_find_errors 0, text_find_denied_leaks 0, at least one sampled chunk found, and the slowest find under 2 s; an incomplete answer (scan cap or a later page) is recorded as text_find_truncated, never a hit. Counts and seconds only; never a word, value, address or citation. live-unverified until a live result exists.
notes: Live-unverified until the live check runs it. Module tests are fixture and injected-transport only: ontology/tests/test_text_index.py (an attachment-only phrase found and cited to its page, withheld records never served, incremental equals cold, a 100k-row text match under 200 ms with work that does not grow with the store, per-reader trim at N=1/10/60) and ontology/tests/test_mail_documents.py (this probe's mail_text_find_checks over FakeWorkbench and FakeGraph, with a leaky variant that grants the mailbox to the withheld reader and must count a leak). It shares ontology.mentions' argv, requires and session state, so in one runner session it reuses the session generation the same way (session_projection.mode incremental) or builds cold once. The vector index is not built (no offline embedding model; the step reports vector unavailable no_offline_embedding_model): plx.find is word-index only. Matching is by word prefix within one 2,000-character chunk, not substring; a sampled chunk whose words are common may honestly be truncated (recorded).
